title: An Evening Bath Prepared at Home
subtheme: An Evening Bath Prepared at Home
description: Warm water, soap, and a towel are ready beside the tub.
cardDescription: Warm water, soap, and a towel are ready beside the tub.
focus: The setting is an Evening Bath Prepared at Home. Match each clue to a thing, action, or description in that scene.
solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Washing the body in a tub
Large open container that can hold water
Faucet controlling the flow of water
Small flat covering used on a floor
Stopper placed in a sink drain
Water vapor rising from a hot kettle

answerNotes.BATH: Bath can mean washing the body or the water prepared for it. The tub is the container rather than the washing activity.
answerNotes.WATER: Water is the same liquid whether it is in a drinking glass, a garden hose, or a cooking pot. The container changes the scene, not the substance.
answerNotes.TAP: Tap can mean a faucet or a light knock. The water-container scene uses the faucet meaning.
answerNotes.SOAP: Soap helps remove dirt when used with water. Rinsing carries away the loosened dirt and remaining suds.
answerNotes.TOWEL: Towels absorb water after washing or swimming. Their looped fabric holds more moisture than a smooth hard surface.
answerNotes.WARM: Warm is a relative temperature word. Something warm has more heat than a cool object but is not usually described as hot.
answerNotes.ROBE: A robe is a loose outer garment. In a Bible story it is clothing, not a separate kind of blanket or tablecloth.

title: Getting Ready for Bed
description: Put on sleepwear and settle a book beside the bed.
cardDescription: Put on sleepwear and settle a book beside the bed.
focus: The setting is getting Ready for Bed. Match each clue to a thing, action, or description in that scene.
solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Usual hour for going to sleep
Soft support for the head in bed
Large soft covering used for warmth
Comfortable footwear worn around the house
Dark time between sunset and dawn
Open the mouth wide when sleepy

answerNotes.BLANKET: A blanket is a covering used for warmth. A quilt usually has several layers held together with stitching.
answerNotes.LAMP: A lamp provides light from a fuel or electrical source. Bible lamps used oil rather than a modern bulb.
answerNotes.BOOK: A book has pages joined inside a cover. The title names the work; the author is the person who wrote it.
answerNotes.ROBE: A robe is a loose outer garment. In a Bible story it is clothing, not a separate kind of blanket or tablecloth.
answerNotes.CLOCK: A clock shows time. The hour hand moves more slowly than the minute hand on a traditional clock face.
answerNotes.NIGHT: Night is the dark part of the daily cycle. Dusk is the fading-light period around the approach of night.
answerNotes.SHEET: Sheet can name paper, bed linen, or a flat baking pan. The scene tells whether the material is paper, cloth, or metal.

solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Small mat placed beneath a drinking glass
Pull-out compartment in a piece of furniture
Reading item with chapters and pages
Take a small mouthful of liquid
Furniture with a flat top and legs

answerNotes.GLASS: Glass is usually transparent but can also be colored. A glass is a drinking vessel, while glass without an article can name the material.
answerNotes.WATER: Water is the same liquid whether it is in a drinking glass, a garden hose, or a cooking pot. The container changes the scene, not the substance.
answerNotes.LAMP: A lamp provides light from a fuel or electrical source. Bible lamps used oil rather than a modern bulb.
answerNotes.DRAWER: A drawer slides in and out of furniture. Its front may have a handle, while dividers separate the contents inside.
answerNotes.BOOK: A book has pages joined inside a cover. The title names the work; the author is the person who wrote it.
answerNotes.CLOCK: A clock shows time. The hour hand moves more slowly than the minute hand on a traditional clock face.
answerNotes.TABLE: A table provides a raised flat surface. Chairs are the separate furniture used to sit beside it.
answerNotes.TOP: A toy top spins on a point. Top can also mean the highest part of an object, so the action in the clue matters.

title: Choosing Comfortable Walking Shoes
description: Notice the laces, sole, and cushioning when choosing a comfortable pair.
cardDescription: Notice the laces, sole, and cushioning when choosing a comfortable pair.
focus: The setting is choosing Comfortable Walking Shoes. Match each clue to a thing, action, or description in that scene.
solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Cord used to fasten a shoe
Outer bottom of a shoe that contacts the ground
Back part of a foot or shoe
Front part of a foot or shoe
Soft pad placed on a reading chair
Material made from treated animal hide

answerNotes.SHOE: A shoe's sole is its bottom surface. The upper covers the foot, and the heel is the raised or rear part.
answerNotes.LACE: A shoelace threads through openings to fasten a shoe. Lace can also name decorative openwork fabric, a different sense.
answerNotes.SOLE: The sole is the shoe's bottom. The tread is the pattern on its outer surface that contacts the ground.
answerNotes.SOCK: A sock covers the foot inside a shoe. Its heel, toe, and cuff name different parts of the same garment.
answerNotes.FOOT: A foot is a body part and also a unit of length. A shoe clue points to the body meaning rather than twelve inches.

solvingTip: Begin with a short answer you recognize. Use its crossing letters to work toward the longer scene words.
words: Put items into a bag or box
Part held when carrying or using something
Carrying band attached to a bag
Fastener closed by pulling a sliding tab
Small folding holder for money and cards
Soft thin wrapping placed around a gift
Small amount of food packed for a break

answerNotes.BAG: A bag is a flexible carrying container. A pocket is generally a smaller compartment attached to clothing or another bag.
answerNotes.HANDLE: A handle is the part made for the hand to grip. Its shape depends on whether the object is carried, pulled, poured, or turned.
answerNotes.KEY: A door key is shaped to match a particular lock. A spare is another key kept for use if the main one is unavailable.
answerNotes.WATER: Water is the same liquid whether it is in a drinking glass, a garden hose, or a cooking pot. The container changes the scene, not the substance.
answerNotes.HAT: A hat covers the head. The brim projects outward, while the crown is the part above it.
